d: A terrible secret threatens Holling and Ruth-Anne's friendship; aspiring pilot Chris is anxious over the written exam.
As Cicely prepares for winter, Joel is puzzled and disturbed when an elderly, but healthy, patient informs him that it is her time to die.
Depressed Shelly flees her baby shower; a Hollywood agent wants Ed to change his script; Chris seeks his feminine side.
Personal secrets are revealed when the northern lights cause the citizens of Cicely to experience one another's dreams.
A musician stalks Maurice, who mulls buying a violin as an investment; Maggie is obsessed with dust mites.
Joel tries to talk down a terminated ranger from his fire tower; Adam ruins Maurice's President's Day fireworks display.
On the day she is to give birth, Shelly sees her child in the future; their relationship frustrates Joel and Maggie.
Friends think Joel is a freeloader, so he throws a dinner party; Chris revises his playlist after a song he played drove a listener crazy.
Joel and Maggie wait out a storm in a secluded cabin, then Ed shows up; Shelly helps Ruth-Anne study Italian.
While fishing, Joel hooks a fabled sea monster; customer demands drive Ruth-Anne to steal Chris' motorcycle; Maurice ridicules Holling's painting.
Joel feels professionally isolated, so Maggie flies in another doctor; Maurice stays with Holling and clan after his furnace explodes.
Maggie hires Maurice to help her build an ultralight, then fires him when he gets bossy; Ed betrays Ruth-Anne's confidence.
Maggie thinks Joel's kindness is making her ill; Maurice tries to duck Ron and Erick's wedding; Holling is the caterer; guest Joyce Van Patten.
Maurice organizes a wheelchair race; Ed helps a contestant; Ted tries to impress Marilyn with a rich client.
Maurice turns a blood drive into a competition with another town while Joel loses his ability to draw blood; one of Maggie's surviving boyfriends visits.
Maurice sneaks a violinist out of a sanitarium to help him woo Semanski; Joel is surprised he is the only one awestruck by his discovery of a frozen mammoth.
Ed videotapes Marilyn's story about a Russian princess, drawing him into a fantasy with his friends playing lead roles.
An ancient Indian herb sends Joel on an out-of-body experience that shows him what his life might have been had he stayed in New York.
Maggie and Maurice regret their donations to a fund-raiser for the library; Miranda's growth depresses Shelly.
Rabbi Schulman takes Joel on a tour of his past, present and future; Maurice tries to impress visiting British royalty.
